newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf Canada to bid for CS Resources.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada to bid for CS Resources.

text.p: Acquisition-hungry Gulf Canada Resources Ltd. said on Friday it would make a C$413 million ($301 million) takeover bid for high-tech Canadian heavy oil producer CS Resources Ltd..

Calgary-based Gulf Canada, which earlier this year acquired Britain's Clyde Petroleum in a bitter fight, said it planned to offer C$14.25 ($10.40) for each CS share in a cash or stock deal that would boost its stake in Canada's booming heavy oil production business.

Serving notice it would not take Gulf's advance lying down, CS, also of Calgary, said it would soon be in a position to unveil a "strategic alliance with an industry partner." It urged shareholders to wait until its board released further information. It did not identify the other company.

It also launched a pre-emptive move before Gulf revealed its intentions on Friday by adopting a shareholder rights plan to increase the time for the company to scout alternative deals to 45 days from the standard 21.
Gulf initiated discussions with CS on May 28 with the aim of hammering out a friendly deal, but Friday's bid was unsolicited, Gulf Chief Executive J.P Bryan said.

"When they announced the adoption of a poison pill that we saw on the wire this morning, we felt we had no choice but to go ahead and make our offer because we feared that the market would see that as a precursor to an offer and the stock would begin to move," Bryan said in an interview.

Shares in CS, whose heavy oil drilling and production operations are concentrated in Alberta and Saskatchewan, were halted early on Friday for the bid news, but jumped C$3.70 to C$15 in busy Toronto Stock Exchange trade when they resumed in early afternoon.
Gulf shares in Toronto were down C45 cents to C$11.90.
Under Gulf's proposal, CS shareholders would be offered either 1.1539 Gulf common shares or all cash, subject to a maximum of C$100 million ($73 million), for each CS share.
The offer represented a 26 percent premium to Thursday's CS closing price of C$11.30 and a 39 percent premium to the closing price of C$10.25 on May 28, Gulf said.
"Based on what we know right now, we've made a bid that we think ought to pre-empt everybody," Bryan said.
But analysts said the Gulf bid appeared to undervalue CS's assets and potential reserves, which were bolstered after a successful drilling program in the first quarter of this year.
Ihor Wasylkiw, analyst with Research Capital Corp., said he valued CS's reported reserves at C$13.56 ($9.89) a share to "somewhere north of C$16 ($11.68)," depending on the accounting method.
"I think there's room for upside," Wasylkiw said.

CS, known for advanced horizontal drilling techniques used under an exclusive license with France's Institut Francais du Petrole, as well as thermal heavy oil recovery, expected to produce 19,500 barrels of oil equivalent a day this year, up from 14,800 last year.

Heavy oil is a thick, gooey form of crude oil that sells at a discount to the light variety because it requires more refining. It is Canada's fastest growing grade of crude and the target of billions of dollars in projects.
